title: Tenant-scoped metric hydration and trace-latching bridge for inference KPIs
creator: Alex Chen
description:
Goal: Build a resilient bridge that hydrates Prometheus-style inference KPIs with tenant-scoped metadata and attaches a stable trace-latch identifier so traces and per-request metrics can be correlated end-to-end across edge, serving runtime, and analytics pipelines.

Motivation: Current KPI collection loses tenant context and per-request trace linkage when requests traverse edge aggregators and per-tenant sharding layers. This causes attribution gaps in latency/error dashboards and forces heavyweight joins in analytics. We need a lightweight, loss-tolerant component that: 1) enriches OTLP metric batches with tenant labels and normalized route/model tags, 2) emits a small, stable trace-latch id as an exemplar which downstream tracing/metrics systems can use to join events, and 3) applies cardinality controls and guardrails to avoid high-cardinality explosions.

Scope:
- Define trace-latch format (stable short id, TTL, deterministic when request id present).
- Implement metric hydration module in edge-aggregator (Go) that: parses incoming OTLP/Prom remote write, injects tenant/model labels, attaches exemplar with trace-latch, enforces label allowlist and sample-rate per tenant.
- Add small header passthrough in serving runtime to accept the trace-latch header and ensure it is present on span creation when available.
- Create an adaptive-limiter that coalesces labels above cardinality thresholds and routes high-cardinality streams to sampled export.
- Update ingestion docs and provide a migration plan for existing dashboards.

Non-goals: Full trace sampling redesign, deep analytics joins (we will provide keys to enable joins, analytics will handle the rest).

Success criteria:
- 95% of inference requests in canary tenants have a trace-latch attached across edge->runtime->ingest path.
- Latency dashboards can attribute 90% of P99 latency spikes to tenant+route without requiring secondary joins.
- No increase in prometheus cardinality beyond 15% for canary tenants (measured by label cardinality).

Risks & Trade-offs:
- Moving hydration to edge reduces bandwidth but increases complexity at the edge layer. We chose edge for lower tail-latency impact vs central enrichers.
- Exemplar-based joins rely on downstream systems supporting exemplars; fallback is to emit compact OTLP metrics with label hints.
- Sampling reduces fidelity for debugging but keeps SLO costs under control. We will tune sample rates per tenant with an opt-in higher fidelity mode for enterprise customers.
comments: 2026-03-05 - Alex Chen: Initial ticket created after SRE + Runtime sync. Recommended prototype in Go sidecar on edge-aggregator. See draft spec in Confluence (attached).

2026-03-07 - Priya Nair: Implemented PoC for trace-latch generation (PR link attached). PoC uses xxhash64 truncated to 12 chars as trace-latch when request-id absent. Need review for collision profile.

2026-03-09 - SRE (Jordan Blake): Reviewed PoC. Concern about lock contention when hydrating high request volume; suggested use of local LRU cache for recent tenant label sets and async exemplar attach path. Also requested metrics for hydration latency (P95).

2026-03-10 - Priya Nair: Updated implementation to async exemplar attach and added LRU cache for tenant metadata; baseline microbenchmark shows <150us median overhead on edge path. Pushed new PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-aggregator/pull/1450
2026-03-11 - Design review (Samira Khan): UX request to expose a dashboard toggle for enterprise tenants to opt into high-fidelity mode. Added to scope for release notes.
2026-03-12 - Paulo (Runtime): Added server-side hook to accept X-Redwood-Trace-Latch header and attach as span attribute. Will send a follow-up PR to runtime repo to include TTL enforcement.

2026-03-12 - Priya Nair: Canary rollout plan drafted. Start with 2 internal tenants for 48 hours (monitor cardinality, ingestion QPS, and P99 metric attribution rate). Rollback criteria: cardinality increase >25% or ingestion error rate >0.5% sustained 15m.
